title: Unit – 2 : Session – 6 : SLO – 1 | Memory Locations and Addresses (1's & 2's Complement)
sections: Section A – Match the Following (Answers)
1. 1's Complement → B. Flip all bits (0→1, 1→0)
2. 2's Complement → A. Add 1 to the 1's complement
3. Signed Number Representation → C. Represents negative numbers in binary
4. Most Significant Bit (MSB) → D. Indicates sign in signed numbers
5. Overflow → E. Error when result exceeds representable range
Section B – Fill in the Blanks
1's complement of a binary number is obtained by FLIPPING ALL BITS.
2's complement of a number is obtained by taking the 1's complement and then ADDING 1.
In 2's complement representation, a negative number always begins with 1 in the MSB.
The range of an 8-bit 2's complement number is from –128 to +127.
When the result exceeds the possible range of values, it causes an OVERFLOW.

Section D – True or False
1's complement is obtained by adding 1 to the binary number. — FALSE
2's complement is the most widely used method for representing signed numbers. — TRUE
In 2's complement, there are two representations for zero. — FALSE (only one)
MSB determines the sign of a signed number. — TRUE
Taking 2's complement twice returns the original number. — TRUE
